en.dek: Microsoft issued an apology and reported progress in restoring Outlook, Teams, and Copilot services following a technical failure that caused disruptions lasting over 18 hours.
body: Microsoft issued an apology on Friday, 13 November 2026, after a global technical failure disrupted its Outlook email services for more than 18 hours. The company stated that affected customers can request service credits for the interruption, according to Variety.

Engineers made progress on Friday in restoring access to email, messaging, and assistant applications following a second day of disruptions, according to reporting by the New York Times and Semafor. Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack as the cause of the issues affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, as reported by the New York Times and El País.

Access to mailboxes stopped for millions of Outlook users starting on Thursday, 12 November 2026. Services began returning to normal after more than 18 hours of continuous disruption, according to El País.

Lawmakers across Europe called for policy changes to lessen reliance on a small group of foreign technology firms after the system failure occurred, according to Politico Europe. The incident led to renewed requests from European officials to reduce dependence on software providers based in the United States.
facts: Microsoft issued an apology on Friday for a technical failure that disrupted Outlook email services worldwide.
The outage left millions of Outlook users without access to mailboxes for more than 18 hours starting on Thursday.
The company ruled out a cyberattack as the cause of the disruptions to Outlook, Teams, and Copilot.
European lawmakers called for measures to reduce reliance on foreign technology companies following the event.
Affected customers can request service credits for the interruption.
en.title: Microsoft Apologizes for Global Outage and Reports Restoration Progress
en.context: The disruptions impacted Microsoft online services worldwide beginning on Thursday, 12 November 2026, before recovery efforts began on Friday.

en.body: Microsoft issued an apology Friday for a worldwide outage of its email servers that left millions of Outlook users without access to their mailboxes starting Thursday in some cases for more than 18 hours. The company said it was due to a technical failure.
en.headline: Microsoft apologizes for worldwide Outlook outage

es.body: Microsoft emitió un viernes un disculpa por una caída global de sus servidores de correo electrónico que dejó a millones de usuarios de Outlook sin acceso a sus buzones desde jueves en algunos casos por más de 18 horas. La compañía indicó que se debió a una falla técnica.
es.headline: Microsoft pide disculpas por una caída global de Outlook

fr.body: Microsoft a présenté ses excuses vendredi pour une panne mondiale de ses serveurs de messagerie qui a privé des millions d'utilisateurs d'Outlook l'accès à leurs boîtes aux lettres, dès jeudi dans certains cas pendant plus de 18 heures. L'entreprise a déclaré qu'il s'agissait d'une défaillance technique.
fr.headline: Microsoft s'excuse pour une panne mondiale d'Outlook

it.body: Microsoft ha emesso un venerdì un'apologia per un'interruzione globale dei suoi server di posta elettronica che ha lasciato milioni di utenti di Outlook senza accesso alle proprie cassette postali a partire da giovedì in alcuni casi per oltre 18 ore. L'azienda ha affermato che è stato dovuto a un guasto tecnico.
it.headline: Microsoft si scusa per l'interruzione globale di Outlook

en.body: Lawmakers across Europe call for action to reduce reliance on a handful of foreign tech companies. The outage renews European calls to detox from US tech.

es.body: Legisladores de toda Europa piden medidas para reducir la dependencia de unas pocas empresas tecnológicas extranjeras. La caída vuelve a avivar en Europa las llamadas a una desintoxicación de la tecnología estadounidense.

fr.body: Des parlementaires à travers l'Europe réclament des mesures pour réduire la dépendance à l'égard d'un petit nombre d'entreprises technologiques étrangères. La panne renouvelle les appels européens à une détox des technologies américaines.
